verdict: Supermicro's sales more than doubled to a record $12.7B, but gross margin squeezed to 6.3% on giant AI deals, so net income rose only modestly to $401M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted; vs $0.51 a year ago; $0.69 non-GAAP

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: vs 11.8% a year ago and 9.3% in Q1 FY26

kpis.label: Cash flow from operations
kpis.note: used in Q2; capex and investments were $46M

segments.name: Total net sales
segments.note: Supermicro reports a single operating segment and printed no product split this quarter. Sales are mostly complete AI server and rack systems built on its Data Center Building Block Solutions.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing next-generation servers, racks and Data Center Building Block Solutions; up 14% YoY.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing; down 8% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Back office, legal and facilities; up 11% YoY.

otherDetail: Interest income of $51.0M plus $0.2M of other income, net, less $25.4M of interest expense — a net $25.9M gain outside operations. A separate $0.5M share of loss from an equity investee, net of taxes, is shown as equityM (amounts from thousands).
oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $90.5M in the quarter — the main gap between GAAP net income ($401M) and non-GAAP net income ($486M, diluted basis).
Management raised the full-year FY26 net sales outlook to at least $40B in this release.
footerNote: Supermicro guided Q3 FY26 net sales to at least $12.3B.

takeaways.title: Sales more than doubled
takeaways.text: Net sales rose to a record $12.7B from $5.7B a year ago on large AI datacenter deployments — more than double Q1's $5.0B in a single step.

takeaways.title: Margins squeezed hard
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 6.3% from 11.8% a year ago as very large AI deals dominated the mix — revenue more than doubled, but gross profit rose only 19%.

takeaways.title: Profit followed, slowly
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $401M from $321M a year ago and $168M in Q1 — real growth, but a fraction of the sales surge, because so little of each sales dollar survived direct costs.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Dec 31, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent below the $3.16 kept as profit — at a 6.3% gross margin, almost every sales dollar goes straight back into building the systems.
